<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let
<MATH_0002>
denote the site studied in Section <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0003>
be a functor, i.e., <MATH_0004> is a presheaf on <MATH_0005>.
In this setting all the axioms [-1],  [0], [1], [2], [3], [4], [5] of
Section <REF_0002> make sense. We will review them
one by one and make sure the reader knows exactly what we mean.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Axiom [-1]. This is a set theoretic condition to be ignored
by readers who are not interested in set theoretic questions.
It makes sense for <MATH_0006> since it concerns the evaluation of
<MATH_0007> on spectra of fields of finite type over <MATH_0008> which are
objects of <MATH_0009>.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
Axiom [0]. This is the axiom that <MATH_0010> is a sheaf
on <MATH_0011>, i.e., satisfies
the sheaf condition for <ACCENT_0001>tale coverings.

<STRUCT_0006><STRUCT_0007>
Axiom [1]. This is the axiom that <MATH_0012> is limit preserving as defined
in Section <REF_0003>:  for any
directed limit of affine schemes <MATH_0013> of
<MATH_0014> we have <MATH_0015>.

<STRUCT_0008><STRUCT_0009>
Axiom [2]. This is the axiom that  <MATH_0016> satisfies the Rim-Schlessinger
condition (RS). Looking at the definition of condition (RS) in
Definition <REF_0004> and the discussion in
Section <REF_0005>
we see that this means: given any pushout <MATH_0017>
of schemes of finite type over <MATH_0018> where <MATH_0019>
are spectra of Artinian local rings, then
<MATH_0020>
is a bijection. This condition makes sense as the schemes
<MATH_0021>, <MATH_0022>, <MATH_0023>, and <MATH_0024> are in <MATHSEG_0001>Noetherian<MATHSEG_0002>
since they are of finite type over <MATH_0025>.

<STRUCT_0010><STRUCT_0011>
Axiom [3]. This is the axiom that every tangent space <MATH_0026>
is finite dimensional. This makes sense as the tangent spaces <MATH_0027>
are constructed from evaluations of <MATH_0028> at <MATH_0029> and
<MATH_0030> with <MATH_0031> a field of finite type over <MATH_0032>
and hence are obtained by evaluating at objects of the category
<MATH_0033>.

<STRUCT_0012><STRUCT_0013>
Axiom [4]. This is axiom that the every formal object is effective.
Looking at the discussion in
Sections <REF_0006> and <REF_0007>
we see that this involves evaluating our functor at Noetherian schemes
only and hence this condition makes sense for <MATH_0034>.

<STRUCT_0014><STRUCT_0015>
Axiom [5]. This is the axiom stating that <MATH_0035> satisfies openness of versality.
Recall that this means the following: Given a scheme <MATH_0036>
locally of finite type over <MATH_0037>, given <MATH_0038>, and given
a finite type point <MATH_0039> such that <MATH_0040> is versal at <MATH_0041>,
then there exists an open neighbourhood <MATH_0042>
such that <MATH_0043> is versal at every finite type point of <MATH_0044>.
As before, verifying this only involves evaluating
our functor at Noetherian schemes.
